title: 2014 HMMT February Guts Problem 5
statement: If four fair six-sided dice are rolled, what is the probability that the lowest number appearing on any die is exactly 3 ?

solutions.text: \(175 / 1296\) The probability that all the die rolls are at least 3 is \(\frac{4^{4}}{6}\). The probability they are all at least 4 is \(\frac{3^{4}}{6}\). The probability of being in the former category but not the latter is thus \(\frac{4}{6}^{4}-\frac{3}{6}^{4}=\frac{256-81}{1296}=\frac{175}{1296}\).
